findings.explanation: Cisco's documented RA Guard drop is a single line with key=value fields: '%SISF-4-PAK_DROP: Message dropped A=FE80::F2F7:55FF:FEBF:F144 G=- V=22 I=Fa1/0/26 P=NDP::RA Reason=Message unauthorized on port'. The text 'RA guard', 'IPv6 SRC:' and 'from port ... interface' never appears. Alert 1's rex extractions and the dataSources filter `Reason:RA guard` would therefore never match.
findings.quote:
%SISF-4-PAK_DROP: from port Gi1/0/15 interface Vlan100,
  Packet dropped, Reason:RA guard policy - rogue router advertisement
  IPv6 SRC: fe80::bad:cafe:dead:beef, IPv6 DST: ff02::1
findings.suggested_fix: Use the real format: filter on "%SISF-4-PAK_DROP" "P=NDP::RA", and extract A= (source address), V= (VLAN) and I= (interface). Check the exact Reason strings for your IOS-XE release in the Cisco System Message Guide.

findings.explanation: Zeek has no icmp.log. ICMP shows up only as summarised flows in conn.log, where the ICMP type sits in id.orig_p, and RA prefix, flags and lifetimes are not logged unless a custom script handles the icmp_router_advertisement event. Every Zeek search here filters on `icmpv6_type=134` and a `prefix=` string that stock Zeek never writes, so the 'secondary detection layer', rate alert, whitelist alert and content-anomaly search have no data.
findings.quote: Zeek generates events in `icmp.log` for ICMPv6 Type 134. Forward to Splunk with `sourcetype=corelight_zeek`.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that RA visibility needs a custom Zeek script (on icmp_router_advertisement) writing a dedicated log, and name that log and its fields. Or use conn.log with proto=icmp and id.orig_p=134 for presence and rate only. Confirm the Corelight/Zeek sourcetype name used by your add-on.

findings.explanation: `protocols router-advertisement ... managed-configuration` makes the Junos device send RAs with the M flag set; it does not guard against rogue RAs. Junos RA Guard is configured under `forwarding-options access-security router-advertisement-guard` (policy, vlans, interface). The `ND_RA_BLOCKED` / `RTADV_GUARD_BLOCKED` syslog tags in dataSources also have no source.
findings.quote:
set protocols router-advertisement interface ge-0/0/0.0 managed-configuration
set switch-options ip-source-guard-enabled
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace with the documented RA Guard configuration (for example `set forwarding-options access-security router-advertisement-guard policy

accept match-list source-mac-address-list ` plus `... vlans policy

`). Look up the actual syslog tag Junos emits for dropped RAs before naming it.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 2812 is the 'EMC XtremIO App for Splunk Enterprise'. Cisco IOS syslog parsing comes from TA-cisco_ios (Splunkbase 1467, deprecated) or its successor, the Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7538).
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Cisco IOS (`Splunk_TA_cisco-ios`, Splunkbase 2812) for SISF/RA Guard syslog.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace it with 'Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk (TA_cisco_catalyst, Splunkbase 7538)', noting legacy TA-cisco_ios (Splunkbase 1467).

findings.explanation: SISF ENTRY_CREATED is logged when a device-tracking binding-table entry is created for a host address. It is not a per-RA 'legitimate RA' event, so counting it as legitimate RAs is likely wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Cisco System Message Guide for SISF-6-ENTRY_CREATED. If it is a binding event, drop it from this UC or describe it as host-binding telemetry.

findings.explanation: No source is given for IOS-XE 16.x as the release that adds RFC 7113 fragment handling, or for a 'reassembly' option in the RA Guard policy. The RA Guard policy has `match ipv6 access-list`, but blocking undetermined-transport fragments is normally a separate IPv6 ACL (`deny ipv6 any any undetermined-transport`).
findings.quote: Fix: upgrade to Cisco IOS-XE 16.x+ which implements RFC 7113 mitigations, and deploy `ipv6 nd raguard policy <name>` with `match ipv6 access-list` and reassembly.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite Cisco's RA Guard / IPv6 FHS configuration guide for the RFC 7113 mitigation, or recommend the undetermined-transport ACL on access ports.

findings.explanation: Kubernetes and Palo Alto have no part in any search, and equipmentModels lists kubernetes_helm. Suricata is mentioned once in implementation with no data source or search.
findings.suggested_fix: Limit equipment to cisco, juniper, zeek and syslog (and remove kubernetes_helm), or add Suricata/PAN data sources and searches.

findings.explanation: The IOS command is `ipv6 nd ra interval` (with a space), as the guide's own configuration shows. The 200-second Cisco default is right.
findings.suggested_fix: Write `ipv6 nd ra interval` (default 200 s on Cisco IOS).

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The "RA guard" and "router-advertisement" keyword filters do not match the real SISF PAK_DROP format (P=NDP::RA, Reason=...). Stock Zeek writes no icmpv6_type field. The VRRP/HSRP MAC exclusion '^(00:00:5e|00:01:00)' covers VRRP but not HSRPv2-IPv6 (00:05:73:a0), and it marks every physically sourced router RA as UNVERIFIED_RA. As written, the search would mostly return nothing.

summary: The threat model and runbook are useful, but the UC's data-collection facts are wrong in several places: the Cisco RA Guard syslog format is invented, Zeek has no icmp.log or icmpv6_type field, the Juniper configuration is not RA Guard, and the Splunkbase ID belongs to an unrelated EMC app. The searches would mostly return nothing, which contradicts `status: verified`.
